films: HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT
beats: Dim bedroom; Poet reads to an averted Ex
Ex falls, Poet follows into clouds
Romantic slow motion and light leaks
Photographs, film and fiction as memory inserts
Floor opens; Poet falls into black
Poet floats in black under flashes
Young Poet watches headlights sweep the room
Parents argue inside a parked car
Object enters chapel through intact window
Empty chapel: pews, choir, baptism pool
Heart floats from shore into Poet
Follow a trail uphill toward the field
Golden plants turn toward Poet; weeds withdraw
Search bare ground for lost hands
Childhood basement, shared mattress, southern wood
Blood and fingerprints carry ancestral power
Voiceover stops; wander toward a house
Bands diverge; home splits; eleven petals
Soul leaves body and watches from above
Overhead Atlantis, blue and pink lights
Angels pour cleansing water over dancing body
Crowds admire Poet; Ex appears and is unreachable
Poet and Ex walk under the moon
Suitcases, phone booth, call to Mother
Mother and Poet watch Poet and Ex break up
Street becomes living room; breakup remains
Mother disappears; Father answers and appears
Father and son walk while breakup persists
Poet touches steel and mounts motorcycle
Ride through Atlantis, buildings and lights streak
Mountain ride, birds and first light
Return to chapel shore and dismount
Modern white temple builds with Poet
Journal becomes blueprint, words are spoken
Completed temple and Poet in sunlight
Friends embrace, laugh and share memories
Walk from temple along harbor to cafe
Couple beside water on Jupiter’s moon
Poet rises from cafe, walks alone
Harbor, temple, Atlantis dissolve into haze
Haze climbs reluctant Poet; float in black
Floating alternates with life’s highs and lows
Return to vintage party in slow motion
Poet disappears into crowd; door closes

wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/01-1.p: What we've made, we don't want. What we've sold — to the world, to ourselves — doesn't exist. I look for a way out: through the hallways, within the drawers, and fire escapes.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/01-2.p: The vape gathers, inside and out. My vision blurs. I move toward the window — and you only get further away. More haze.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/01-3.p: It was the maze, constructed by a tainted love. You fall off the fire escape, into darkness — and the city streaks upward like it's leaving too.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/01-4.p: I trip on my own words, falling out of life — and find where you go when you leave. The gap between us breathes, and never closes.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/02-1.p: It was the type of silent scream a trapped lover makes to escape: a pending marriage, a concussion, a set of walls caving inward.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/02-2.p: An emergency call while tossing and turning — the silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight, to digest a truth.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/02-3.p: A winless insomnia. An epiphany of a road winding down. My eyes dilate — and we go through.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/02-4.p: I was six, I recall, when the ghost of a dead and love-less seven-year-old appeared, and shared that my parents' marriage wouldn't last. A warm, heavy breeze in winter, where a child is left home alone.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/02-5.p: Curtains pulled, and blinds up as far and as wise as possible — to see flashing lights, and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/02-6.p: And no tears, and no fucks, and no love to give. The ghost hands me a tambourine — and I throw it through the window.

It thunders. Then rains until nothing remains. What was once love, now goods — broken and sealed apart by lightning. Daily breads, soaked and delivered rotted by rain; and blankets, soiled by venomous puppeteers.

Ode to the storm ending. Ode to two sets of mud-imprinted footsteps, leading away from what the water kept.

And a tambourine, shattered into pieces. What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore?
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/04-1.p: What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore — and the ashes of expired wildfires cover sands, and debris lifted from the night sea water’s floor.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/04-2.p: The waves calm to folded whispers; the winds mute the trees. The right level of silence, to find a throbbing heart — it used to be mine. I lift it with care: nevermore.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/04-3.p: What if I followed this reclaimed heart, to where the puzzle pieces of faith are handcrafted — scrambled and scattered as mustard seeds into the vast moonlit night’s garden fields.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/04-4.p: The plants in a golden hue bloom, and face toward me in anticipation. The weeds repel, falling into the shadows where our memories hide — and mean so little, in a moment of defeat — as I’m called forward.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/04-5.p: The clouds mute the stars for the deepest level of darkness — welcoming extra hard work, to search the bare ground for two hands.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/04-6.p: Hands that once could touch dust after dusk, and feel good — they too used to be mine. I put them back on, with the care of my future at stake: nevermore.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/05-1.p: Now go, they tell me. To ask if I can inherit the earth — to ask if I can name my own stars. Even galaxies, if I may.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/05-2.p: The past, too, was waiting for me — coming of age in the shared rooms of humid basements as bedrooms; mattress pads where the wood beams of Southern pine could comfort my spine. It didn’t. To dream was to prevail.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/05-3.p: They tell me: ask if I can invent a new universe — if God would let me, little ole me, award a blessing here and there. Even grant miracles.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/05-4.p: In uncertain times, in forsaken times. Their blood flows through my hands — fingerprints that orchestra great powers — sun-kissing my skin, deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries. Beware of me.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/05-5.p: The gates open with wings — gifted from evolution, and made of marble stones kissed by the hymns our Creator composed, with an orchestra of our ancestors’ wildest dreams, to welcome us.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/06-1.p: Poets, who eased generations down yellow brick roads — and plucked our souls out of their secret places, to follow comets to the capital city of our collective consciousness.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/06-2.p: Resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one — the pact we've made here with nature, abandoned and hoped for the best, back on life.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/06-3.p: A relearned currency, we reassess as the admission. But here we are all safe. An unfamiliar, flickering candle light, illuminating smiles at night.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/06-4.p: Where shadows cast from narrow streets beaming with love — in the joyful noises that color rainbows, and give us infinite time to heal, and set clouds free.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/06-5.p: I know my soul — and it could stay here forever. Leaving behind crosshairs for continuums, and strains for serendipity.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/06-6.p: A city born in unison, out of the purest of fictions — welcoming me, and welcoming all.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-1.p: DJ, turn me up, please. Eyes wide shut, chin nested at the arch of the weight of these spoken words.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-2.p: I have a love story to tell — of ghosts, whispering unfolded dilutions, birthed in purity, and dying in the vineyards of sun-soaked evergreen fields, unnourished.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-3.p: One by one, treasures escaping — devaluing themselves after unsullied stars diminished their glares. I walked a thousand light years to be heard. So DJ — please — turn me up.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-4.p: So I can speak: of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a shared home, boxed and trucked on separate one-way streets — not built with U-turns, or stop, maybe-we-shouldn't signs.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-5.p: A love story of years — eleven years — each plunkled off as daisy petals. We love, we not. Of a future gone swiftly, and a past left empty-handed.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-6.p: To pick a road: of heavy rain. Or of frontal fog. Or of dimmed night lights under a cloud — with a silver lining.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/07-7.p: Now, turning forth to face delights and shadows — one night at a time; one tear at a time; one open mic at a time. Chin now nested high, and volume turnt up.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-1.p: Pulsing, and head throbbing from the music — and empty, on a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-2.p: The soul escapes my body, and leaves him on the dance floor — just flesh and bones. Rejection and heartache hit different, with no feelings afloat.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-3.p: I want my soul to imagine my body. Watch strangers collide and spark electric currents that gamut the mood. We want him to be the last to leave.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-4.p: Now let us put my soul in the middle of an open field — at the equator of a planet much larger than my own, and much hotter.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-5.p: Cool me down: pouring unfiltered water out of ice baths, salted from the closest moons, from angles of the newest religions — their graces curse or bless me. Only infinity will tell.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-6.p: Now bring my soul back to my body: to lean back, breathe in the smoke that fills the room — how good it is to finally get acquainted with the night.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/08-7.p: Unfamiliar, yet relatable mountains in the distance; wandering thoughts within reach. Accepting you'll never say, nor feel, my love was real. What isn't mine, I still can not give.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/09-1.p: Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it. We talk for years, travel through time — we grow old together, I believe. Maybe we could have it all.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/09-2.p: Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she's never known. We talk for years, re-closet wounds, and re-explain my way of birth. Even after prayer: what isn't mine, I still can not give.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/09-3.p: Before I go, I call on my father — his calming demeanor summoned from the yonders. We walk for years, east toward the sunrises, retracing his footsteps — my tears falling in the wave shadows of the inner harbor.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/09-4.p: We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken. Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/10-1.p: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are — blissful, and oddly sensitive. I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings, and hop on.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/10-2.p: Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell — being everywhere, with no one to love. I let the noise block the noise. The way I ride: eyes turn, heads twist — and prove the magic still exists.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/10-3.p: All preparations to live and dream in darkness, I no longer desire. The moon settles, and the tease of distant stars subsides — and I can see a morning ahead for me.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/10-4.p: It looks like a morning I could believe in — a morning where loss and life aren't so — well — ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm. The chirping of birds, fueling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/10-5.p: With my own curiosities, for a chance at an end wherever everything will be OK. I want to live in this feeling forever — blissful, and oddly innocent.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/10-6.p: Riding in a way you can't help but double-click — and prove the magic still exists. Even here, it's chilly in the morning.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/11-1.p: Fog covers the seas and hugs the tree-covered hills, floating through the morning as it exhales its introduction. This world is at peace.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/11-2.p: In the awakening of dawn, in fresh muted colors: we can rebuild this temple. It's a new day — a catharsis for me to say, with newfound energies and recycled airs.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/11-3.p: We can rebuild this temple — under vibrant sun rays of glory, of the wisdoms of morning dews and their winks of luck.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/11-4.p: With laps around infinity pools of edgeless dreams, that reflect the enormity of the skies.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/11-5.p: And of modern faiths — that we too can walk on water. Deep breaths, in appreciation of present life, and our present positions.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/11-6.p: We can rebuild this temple. It's a new day. A catharsis. We can welcome a new day.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/12-1.p: Decades later, there is less time for words, and more space for laughter — hugs with no reason, and loud voices, so our hearts can be overheard.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/12-2.p: Less time for words. More space for laughter.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/12-3.p: Reflecting on legacies, and creeds once told — of elders, now past.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/12-4.p: And is this a one-time occasion? we ask. Or will we make time, in the sands of burning hourglasses?
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/12-5.p: Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/13-1.p: Find me at the harbor, at the small tables, watching.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/13-2.p: The couples orbit each other the way Jupiter keeps its moons — close, and counted.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/13-3.p: The elders clutch their pearls and pray. Life has burned all my love stories — victory-less seasons.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/13-4.p: So I harvest the flowers instead — scarlet poppies, purple blossoms — and they become my power.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/13-5.p: Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/13-6.p: Don't make me leave. I escaped here for a reason.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/14-1.p: A hot minute. The haze gathers on the water — and everything I built here learns to be weather: the city, the temple, the harbor.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/14-2.p: It takes me last, and from the ground up. I am reluctant — but I have been weather before.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/14-3.p: All black again. But no walls this time.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/14-4.p: A life flashes the way a reel does: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars, the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/14-5.p: Our dance together is a victory — two entwined muses, as it ends.
wygwyl/Halfworld_Reference_Frames/14-6.p: An old door, from a vintage somewhere. It opens on a slow party — the kind I once fell out of a window to escape. This time, I choose the door.
